macro.stance: Constructive on physical infrastructure, but increasingly barbelled: power/grid, cooling/water and quality nuclear remain structural winners, while oil/refining is a tactical geopolitical hedge rather than a clean demand signal.
marketContext: Monday Asia trading opened with Brent around $88.72 and WTI around $82.35 as U.S.-Iran talks remained stalled and Hormuz shipping slowed sharply; crude had risen more than 5% in the prior week.

The more acute energy bottleneck remains refined products: refinery constraints and disrupted trade routes have kept crack spreads unusually elevated even while crude itself is not accelerating proportionally.
The latest Live Desk context was generated August 16 but its theme states remain stale/neutral, so no conviction change in this packet is attributed to the overlay.

ism.status: July 2026 remains the latest official ISM Manufacturing and Services dataset. The existing snapshot was re-verified and intentionally not rewritten because no new monthly report exists.
ism.nextOfficialRelease: August 2026 Manufacturing is due September 1 and Services September 3.
ism.interpretation: The July signal still favours physical bottlenecks: strong manufacturing orders/production/backlog, low customer inventories and shortages in electrical/electronic components, switchgear, transformers, wire/cable and memory. This supports grid equipment, cooling, automation and industrial suppliers with pricing power.

categoryReads.why: Gas-turbine and electrical-equipment order intensity remains exceptional. Recent industry data put Q2 global gas-turbine orders near 38 GW, up roughly 71% year over year, reinforcing GEV/ETN/HUBB/PWR/POWL rather than requiring another duplicate ticker.

ECL, MOD and XYL now provide differentiated exposure across direct liquid cooling, chillers, ultrapure water, reuse and municipal/industrial water infrastructure. Ecolab's CoolIT acquisition and Modine's hyperscaler agreement make cooling a genuine AI infrastructure layer rather than an ESG side theme.
Prefer power distribution, thermal management, networking and water systems over adding more undifferentiated compute beta. Existing VRT/ETN/NVT/FIX/NET plus new MOD/ECL cover distinct bottlenecks.
No fresh issuer disclosure today displaces BWXT/CCJ/LEU/CGN Power from the preferred quality/fuel-cycle stack. Development-stage reactor names remain speculative.

categoryReads.change: Geopolitical risk strengthened; demand signal still mixed
categoryReads.why: Hormuz traffic slowed sharply and peace talks remain stalled, but crude is not reflecting an unconstrained shortage. Maintain XOM/CVX/CNOOC and gas infrastructure; refiners remain tactical beneficiaries of unusually tight product markets.
Electrical buildout, cooling systems, grid capex and data centres all reinforce copper intensity. No additional miner cleared the diversification bar today.

Unitree's extreme IPO demand confirms investor appetite but also valuation risk. Commercial evidence still favours warehouse/fixed automation first, cobots/mobile manipulation second, industrial humanoids third and general-purpose humanoids last.

Prefer productivity and water-efficiency exposure over commodity processors: CTVA for seeds/crop protection and VMI for precision irrigation plus grid crossover. Agriculture cyclicality prevents higher conviction today.

LLY and DXCM provide differentiated exposure to obesity/type-2 diabetes and chronic metabolic disease through therapeutics and monitoring. Treat this as a long-duration health-demand theme, not a simplistic cheap-food proxy.

Existing TNB, Southern Cable, YTL Power, SunCon and MN Holdings already capture the strongest grid/data-centre construction exposures. Water/cooling is a research gap for Bursa and should be screened separately rather than forcing a weak local proxy.
Maintain 0836.HK, 1816.HK, 1072.HK and Geekplus. Unitree's scarcity valuation is too aggressive to displace cheaper operating infrastructure/automation exposures.

companyChanges.reason: Best cross-theme water + AI-cooling platform after CoolIT; direct liquid cooling plus ultrapure/process water is differentiated from existing electrical infrastructure names.
Data-centre sales growth and the $4bn long-term hyperscaler chiller agreement support a high-growth cooling thesis, but customer concentration and capex execution keep risk above ECL/XYL.
Q2 orders +42% and broad water/reuse exposure make it the lower-AI-beta water-security compounder.
Gas-turbine and grid-equipment scarcity remain intact; no new contradiction.
Metabolic-disease demand remains structural, but valuation and competitive pipeline risk prevent an upgrade.
